subject: Re: Discovery - model fit & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-25T15:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery - model fit & next steps

Thanks for the time today, Jordan — great conversation. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery call focusing on model fit and evals for the Acme search summarization flow:

- Current ask: Improve factuality and reduce hallucinations in long-document summarization for search results (typical docs ~3-10k tokens).
- Immediate recommendation: Pin to Redwood model rwd-llama-medium@v2.0 for consistency while we run a targeted eval suite; rwd-llama-large@v2.1 shows better latency/cost but we noticed potential quality drift on your canonical prompts.
- Deliverables we agreed on:
  1) Share the eval benchmark we discussed (PDF) + the prompt set v2 you provided.
  2) Run a head-to-head diff between v2.0 and v2.1 on your prompt set and sample of production data.
  3) Propose an action (rollback, pin, or targeted prompt tuning) within 48 business hours depending on results.

I've attached the eval report and the cleaned prompt set we used during the call. Next steps from my end: three things by EOD tomorrow — full diff report, recommended mitigation, and a proposed rollback runbook if you want to revert to v2.0.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: acme_eval_report.pdf] [Attachment: prompt_set_v2.jsonl]

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@acme.ai>
Date: 2026-06-25T17:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery - model fit & next steps

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the recap. Quick flag: after our internal test yesterday we saw a regression in factuality when Acme pinned to rwd-llama-large@v2.1 (the model you demoed). Example below (sensitive data redacted):

---
Input: "Summarize section 4 of contract ABC-123"
v2.0 output: "Section 4 requires delivery within 60 days and retains supplier liability for defects."
v2.1 output: "Section 4 requires delivery within 30 days and transfers liability to the buyer."
---

This kind of difference is a blocker for us. We need to avoid shipping any version that changes contractual obligations. Can you confirm next steps and whether we can pin back to v2.0 immediately? Also copying procurement — they may want an official timeline for any rollback.

Jordan
Senior PM, Search | Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-26T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery - model fit & next steps

Jordan — thanks for the concrete example, that's exactly the kind of regression we want to triage immediately. Short answer: yes, we can mitigate quickly. Proposed plan:

1) Immediate mitigation (hours): Pin your production routing to rwd-llama-medium@v2.0 — this will freeze behavior while we investigate. Pinning is non-disruptive and preserves your existing traffic routing.
2) Short investigation (24-48 hrs): Our eval team will run a diff report on your prompt_set_v2.jsonl + a 500-sample production subset. We'll produce a side-by-side scoring on factuality, hallucination rate, and ROUGE/factual precision. Link to the running benchmark is below.
3) Remediation (48-96 hrs): If diff shows systemic regression, options are rollback (full revert of rwd-llama-large@v2.1 to previous variant in your dedicated pool), targeted prompt tuning, or allowlist of prompts to route to v2.0.

Attachments and links:
- Running benchmark: https://redwood-inference.app/benchmarks/acme-eval-2026
- Prompt set we used: https://docs.redwood-inference.com/prompt-sets/acme/prompt_set_v2
- [Attachment: acme_eval_report.pdf] (first-pass)

Can you confirm you want us to pin to v2.0 now? If so I will open the rollback/pinning ticket and include estimated timeline.

Best,
Marissa

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-27T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery - model fit & next steps

Looping in ops details. TL;DR: we can pin or rollback depending on Acme preference. Technical notes:

- Pin: We will update routing rules to force model id rwd-llama-medium@v2.0 for the production route in your tenant. This typically takes ~30 minutes to propagate and has zero data migration risk.
- Full rollback of v2.1 for your dedicated pool: we can revert the deployed model variant in ~4 hours (includes smoke tests). Impact: short window of reduced capacity while we redeploy; we'll schedule during low-traffic if you prefer.
- Canary: If you want to validate fixes, we recommend a canary (5-10% traffic) on v2.1 with heavy monitoring for hallucination/factuality metrics.

I've attached the rollback runbook we use for these situations. If Acme confirms "Pin now" we'll do that and run the diff in parallel, then propose a remediation path.

Regards,
Vivek
Head of Reliability | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: rollback_runbook.md]

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.ai>

Thanks Vivek — please proceed with pinning to rwd-llama-medium@v2.0 immediately. Procurement: we may need a short notice or amendment to the SLA if the rollback impacts throughput — procurement team, can you confirm constraints?

Marissa: once pinned, please share the diff report and an ETA for a follow-up call to review remediation options (prompt tuning vs. rollback). Prefer timeline within 48 business hours.

Jordan

- Running diff: the eval team has started the side-by-side run (500 sample) and will deliver a report by EOD tomorrow. Link: https://redwood-inference.app/benchmarks/acme-eval-2026
